title: Her age, arthritis and feeling 16
summary: She jokes about boyfriends and her children, mentions arthritis and a cane, and says being active keeps her feeling sixteen at eighty.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: (Unintelligible) somebody promised to be. I got a whole lot of people promised to be. But I got children, I can't have no boyfriends because of my children. They're watching you every -- I ________ me in the bed with a man there. They come there (unintelligible). I say, they think they smart, but they ain't smart. (Unintelligible) all the time, tipping, making out you're going to the bathroom. But they ain't got no business in my room because they ain't got not a thing in there, not even ________.
You feel good and strong and vigorous?
Uh-huh. (Unintelligible) and that's my legs act up (inaudible).

Yeah. I go with this cane and I leave it sitting there. I say, "Where's my cane?" I go hunting for it. But I have to have it to go down the steps. I say, "Go hunt for my cane." I send the children to go looking for the cane. But it's so often I go to the bathroom and go get something to eat (unintelligible) don't know where it is. It goes south somewhere.
So you don't use the cane all the time?
I use it to go down the steps. Anything else be -- you know. But (unintelligible) to go faster. I use it to go faster. (Unintelligible). I can't ride no bus.
Ma Rainey wasn't working when she was 80 years old, was she? Was she working at that age?
Making records still? You think she was 80? You think she was --
(unintelligible) when I'm 80. Well, I'm 80 now, but I don't know what age she was at that time. But see, I'm 80 now. See, (Unintelligible). But I feel like I'm 16.
I think that's wonderful. Why do you feel like you're 16? What do you think?
You feel like you're 16 because you're playing and singing all the time?
